📡 US targets two fishing boats off Qeshm; two crew members missing

📌 Bandar Abbas, IRNA – An attack by the US military on two fishing boats in waters off Qeshm Island, southern Iran, has left two crew members missing, Hormozgan Province Deputy Governor Ahmad Nafisi says.

The incident occurred at about 11:30 a.m. local time on Saturday, 18 nautical miles from Messen village in Qeshm County. Each boat had two people on board, Nafisi said, according to the provincial governor’s public relations office.
​
Two crew members were brought to Qeshm, he said, adding that one was injured and taken to hospital for treatment.
​
The other two remain missing, and search and rescue operations in the area are underway, Nafisi said, noting that authorities were following up and would release further details after receiving verified reports.

A data leak has linked the real identities of 291 crypto users directly to their wallet activity, stripping away the anonymity they relied on.

The breach highlights a persistent vulnerability in crypto: while blockchain transactions can be pseudonymous, KYC and compliance records held by centralized services create a paper trail that, if exposed, can permanently de-anonymize users.

🖥 Iran ready to join three initiatives at COP17 on biodiversity conservation

📌 Tehran, IRNA – Iran has expressed readiness to join three initiatives launched at the proposal of the presidency of the 17th Conference of the Parties to the Convention on Biological Diversity (CBD COP 17), which focus on biodiversity monitoring, mountain and freshwater ecosystems, and areas supporting conservation.

According to Iran’s Department of Environment, deputy head for natural environment and biodiversity Hamid Zahrabi conveyed the Islamic Republic’s interest in the initiatives in a letter to Armenia’s environment minister, who chairs CBD COP 17.
​
One initiative proposes a Yerevan Biodiversity Technology and Monitoring Hub to help countries access monitoring tools and promote closer cooperation among participating countries. A second seeks to establish a Mountain and Freshwater Platform, highlighting mountain habitats and their role in supplying freshwater.
​
The third initiative concerns an Action Hub for Other Effective Area-based Conservation Measures (OECMs). These are areas managed for purposes other than biodiversity protection but whose safeguards also benefit nature. Examples include the surroundings of historical sites and certain agricultural and livestock areas.
​
In his letter, Zahrabi reaffirmed Iran’s commitment to Target 18 of the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework. The target calls on countries, in line with national circumstances and priorities, to reduce subsidies harmful to biodiversity and redirect them toward supportive activities.
​
COP17 takes place in Yerevan from October 18 to 31, 2026. Participants assess progress under the framework and discuss ways to accelerate conservation, mobilize funding, and strengthen international cooperation.
